```markdown
# release-notes: breaking-change flag

Source: deferred item 7 in `specs/deferred_items.md`.

## Intent and why

Breaking changes must be easy to see. Two readers act on them:

- A person who reads the release notes must see breaking changes at a glance.
- `announce` must put breaking changes first in its post.

## Current state

- `release-notes` writes one bullet for each merged pull request.
- `skills/changelog-check/parse.py` splits each bullet on " — ". It rejects a bullet with more than two parts.
- `announce` reads the parsed entries to build its post.

## Goals

1. `release-notes` marks a bullet as breaking when its pull request is breaking.
2. `parse.py` accepts the mark and records it on the entry.
3. `announce` lists breaking entries before all other entries.

## Non-goals

- No other change to the bullet format.
- No rewrite of old release notes.
- No detection of breaking changes from code or commit text. The pull request label is the only source.

## Anti-goals

- Old release notes have no tag. If any of them stops parsing, or parses differently, this work has failed.

## Constraints

- The " — " separator stays.
- The two-part limit in `parse.py` stays for the text after the tag.

## Approaches

| Approach | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| 1. Add " — breaking: yes" as a third part | `parse.py` must accept three parts. This loosens the format check for all bullets. |
| 2. Start the bullet with a `[breaking]` tag | `parse.py` removes the tag before it splits. Bullets without the tag parse exactly as before. |

The partner picked approach 2. Reason: older notes stay valid with no change.

## Design (agreed in conversation)

- `release-notes`: when the merged pull request has the `breaking` label, start its bullet with `[breaking]`.
- `parse.py`: when a bullet starts with `[breaking]`, remove the tag and set `breaking=True` on the entry. Then split the rest as today.
- `announce`: list breaking entries first.
- Test in `skills/changelog-check/`: one bullet with the tag and one bullet without it.

## My calls (not discussed with the partner)

- An untagged entry gets `breaking=False`, so every entry has the field.
- The tag match is exact and case-sensitive: `[breaking]`.
- The tag goes directly after the list marker, for example `- [breaking] ...`.
- `announce` keeps the current order inside each group (breaking, then the rest).

## Left to the builder

- Where `breaking` lives on the parsed entry type, following the current code in `parse.py`.
- How `announce` reads the field, following its current parse step.
```

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The leading tag is safe because `parse.py` checks the *number of parts* after the " — " split. A prefix removed before the split never reaches that check, so the two-part rule stays strict.
- The `breaking` label on the pull request is the single source of truth. `release-notes` translates it into text, and the other two skills only read that text. No skill needs access to GitHub labels except the one that writes the notes.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I wrote the design to `specs/release-notes-breaking-flag.md`. It contains what we agreed, plus a short "My calls" section with choices I made on my own. One example: `announce` keeps the current order inside the breaking group.
